properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 7:47PM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Plaskett burn area in...
South Central Monterey County in central California...

* Until 1000 PM PST.

* At 747 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Plaskett Burn Area. Between 2 and 5
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Plaskett Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Plaskett Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile marker 11 including
Los Burros Road.
properties.instruction:
Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Los Burros Road, areas near Plaskett
Creek Campground and structures along the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 7:46PM PST until November 18 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Timber burn area in...
Western Monterey County in central California...

* Until 1000 PM PST.

* At 746 PM PST, CHP has reported an observed debris flow into NB
Highway One lanes in the vicinity of Big Sur Lodge and boulders in
the roadway at Hurricane Point. A car was reported stuck in the
debris flow near Big Sur. Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated that heavy rain was falling over the Timber Burn Area.
Between 3 and 6 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall
rate is 0.5 to 0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area. Conditions remain
favorable for additional moderate to heavy rainfall due to
orographic lift as the main rainband exits the county. Flash
flooding is ongoing. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will
result in debris flow moving through the Drainages within Lafler,
Castro and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between Grimes and
Castro Canyons. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Timber Burn Area.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Timber Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from
Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of
Big Sur.

At 5:43 PM PST CHP reported a debris flow across NB Highway 1 lanes
in the vicinity of Big Sur Lodge. One hour rain rates have crossed
0.7" with additional heavy rain expected this evening into tomorrow
as scattered showers with the potential for moderate to heavy rain
and thunderstorms. CHP additionally reported boulders in the NB lane
of Highway One at Hurricane Point at 6:11 PM local time. CHP reported
a car stuck in the debris flow at Big Sur.
properties.instruction:
Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Highway 1 near mile marker 50 south of
Andrew Molera State Park to mile maker 38. Other areas impacted
include Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park Campground and Partington Ridge,
structures along the Big Sur River, Mule Creek Canyon, and adjacent
drainages and watershed outlets.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 18 at 10:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Ongoing extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage.
Additional heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours will continue to
produce river rises, bringing record flood levels at this point
overnight Thursday into Friday morning. this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This is forecast to approach and surpass the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 17.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:15 PM EST Wednesday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1115 AM EST.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin

* WHEN...Until 445 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,

possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1253 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 9:10 AM
Wed 11/18, 1.3 ft above normal (6.2 ft MLLW) at 9:41 AM Thu
11/19, 1.6 ft above normal (6.5 ft MLLW) at 10:07 AM Fri
11/20, and 2.0 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 10:32 AM Sat
11/21.
* West Sacramento: 1.4 ft above normal (5.7 ft MLLW) at 12:09
PM Wed 11/18, 1.6 ft above normal (6.0 ft MLLW) at 12:37 PM
Thu 11/19, 1.9 ft above normal (6.3 ft MLLW) at 1:04 PM Fri
11/20, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 1:35 PM Sat
11/21.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +6.5 ft at 11:00 AM Wed 11/18,
+6.9 ft at 12:00 PM Thu 11/19, +6.4 ft at 12:00 PM Fri 11/20,
and +6.8 ft at 1:00 PM Sat 11/21.
- These predictions include up to +2.1 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:

tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.
